what: The entry gate (logo, intro, button) waits 1s, then fades in over 1s, and scrolling is locked meanwhile. Pressing the button returns to the top and the gate fades out over 1s. 1s later a viewport-height title panel fades in over 1s and the subtitle fades in 1s after it. After another 2.2s the title panel’s min-height collapses from window height to 0 over 2s, pushing the body below upward, and 4.5s after the press scroll unlocks (all ease-in-out). fx:enter fires on press and fx:done fires on unlock

options.wait: Wait before the door lights up (sec), default 1
options.fade: Door open and closed duration (s), default 1 — the title starts after it closes
options.sub: How late the subtitle follows the title (s), default 1
options.fold: Extra delay (sec) before folding after the title starts, default 2.2
options.unlock: When scroll is released after pressing (s), default 4.5
options.lock: If false, does not lock scrolling
options.remove: false hides the closed door with display:none only instead of removing it from the document (the default removes it like the original — and puts it back in place when reattached)
options.[data-fx-part=gate]: Door — panel covering the screen (position and size set by the consuming CSS)
options.[data-fx-part=head]: Title panel — stands at window height at first, then folds (optional)
options.[data-fx-part=rest]: Body — shows right after the door fades out (optional)

note: The original removes the door after 1s with react state and lights the title with CSS keyframes. This motion part uses GSAP to produce the same length and curve. The title panel height is innerHeight px rather than 100vh as in the original (one screen even when the phone address bar changes). With reduced motion the door is visible from the start, and pressing it opens everything at once
